Therefore, over the life of the mine, agricultural production equivalent to 25,000 acres multiplied by seven years at a minimum will be foregone, although the acreage out of production at any given time will be limited. At the low level of development peak annual production rates of 15 million tons on Tract III and 4 million tons on Tract II, the approximate acreage involved in mining and reclamation at any given time would be about 2,750 acres, or about 9 percent of the total acreage of the Tracts. Peak annual production rates at the high level of development (26 mtpy) will result in about 4,011 acres (13 percent of the total acreage of the tracts)
In 1975, approximately 2,275 acres or 7 percent of the area on Tracts II and III, was under cultivation. Seven years of foregone agricultural income on this acreage is estimated to be about $483,000 over the life of the operations.
It requires approximately 3 acres to support a cow and calf for 1 month in the Sarpy Creek area. If 2,750 acres were idle at the low level rate of production, 917 animal unit months, or enough grass to support 92 animal units for a 10 month period would be lost annually due to the mining activity. At the high level rate of production about 134 animal units would be lost annually to mining.
Foregone grazing production on 22,725 acres of grazing land to be mined over the life of the operation is estimated to be about 5,250 animal units at the low level and 7,236 at the high level.
